# Ball Trajectory Analysis

## Initial Conditions
The ball starts near the **top center** of the playing field (approximately x≈400).

## Tracing the Path

### Step 1: First Line (Upper-Left to Center-Right)
The ball falls and hits the **first diagonal line**, which slopes gently **down to the right** (from ~x=55 to ~x=530). The ball gains rightward velocity and slides to the right end of this line.

### Step 2: Transition to Second Line
After sliding off the right end of Line 1 (~x=530, y≈150), the ball drops a very short distance onto the **second upper line**, which runs from center-left (~x=285) up to the upper-right (~x=730). This line slopes **upward to the right**.

### Step 3: Redirection Left
Since Line 2 slopes uphill to the right, the ball **reverses direction** and slides **leftward** down the slope. It reaches the left end of Line 2 at approximately (x≈285, y≈210) and falls off.

### Step 4: Lower-Left Diagonal Line
The ball, now carrying leftward momentum, falls and lands on the **lower-left diagonal line** (running from the left wall down toward center-bottom). This line slopes **down to the right**, so the ball slides rightward along it.

### Step 5: Final Drop
The ball exits Line 3 at approximately **x≈370–400**, which is directly above the **center bucket**. With moderate rightward velocity, it falls into the gap between the lower lines and drops into **Bucket 2**.

## Key Insight
The second upper line acts as a **deflector**, reversing the ball's rightward motion. The lower-left line then redirects the ball back toward center, funneling it precisely over Bucket 2.
